title: AVL Trees: The First Self-Balancing Search Tree (1962)
explainer: Soviet mathematicians Georgy Adelson-Velsky and Evgenii Landis published the AVL tree in 1962, generally credited as the first self-balancing binary search tree. Their rule - that the heights of a node's two subtrees may never differ by more than one - set the template that later balanced-tree designs adapted, making it a useful reference point for the balancing strategies this lesson covers.

title: B-Trees and the Problem of Disk-Based Storage (circa 1970)
explainer: Rudolf Bayer and Edward McCreight developed the B-tree at Boeing Research Labs, with their work circulating around 1970, to solve a problem in-memory trees don't face: minimizing slow disk reads when an index is too large to fit in memory. That disk-oriented design is why B-trees and their variants, rather than plain binary search trees, underlie most databases and filesystems today.
